issues.title: Invalid proof of the all-s tubular scaling lemma
issues.failure_explanation: The asserted embedding estimate is invalid for all s>1/2. For example, at s=2 it would give a 3/2-Hölder difference bound for any smooth nonconstant function supported in the positive half-interval, which fails near a point where its derivative is nonzero. The proof also explicitly omits 0<s<=1/2 and does not prove the averaged normal-fiber restriction needed in higher dimensions. Thus the lemma's statement for every s>0 is unsupported, even though the full inequality is not thereby shown false.
issues.overall_effect: The residual estimates in all three error theorems rely on this lemma. In particular, the p=1 case uses the omitted low-fractional range, so the old theorem chain is not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the invalid Hölder-embedding argument with valid one-dimensional support-Poincaré/Hardy estimates and an averaged normal-slicing estimate in tubular coordinates. A complete contained repair may restrict the lemma to 0<s<1/2 and positive integer s, choose 0<ε<1/2 for p=1 and s=p−1 for p≥2, and recheck the residual terms in the energy, H1, and L2 proofs; these ranges cover every use and preserve the theorem rates. Any retained all-s formulation must instead be proved in the omitted noninteger ranges.
issues.why_classification: The false embedding and the omitted low-fractional and higher-dimensional arguments are genuine analytic gaps requiring a nontrivial replacement proof and an auxiliary slicing result. The work is nevertheless confined to this lemma and its residual applications, and a comparable lemma sufficient for the entire theorem chain survives without loss of the advertised convergence orders.

issues.title: Unsupported residual compatibility of the load extension

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Such an extension can for instance be obtained using the extension operator in \eqref{eq:ext-stab}.

issues.failure_explanation: The old assumption controls the Sobolev norm of f_delta but imposes no relation between f_delta and the separately chosen extension u^e outside Omega. Thus it does not imply that the H^s norm of Delta u^e+f_delta in the tubular neighborhood is controlled solely by the local H^{s+2} norm of u^e. For instance, when u and f vanish near the boundary, an otherwise stable nonlocal extension of interior f may have nonzero exterior values while the asserted right-hand side is zero. The last inequality in the residual estimate is therefore an unestablished premise.
issues.overall_effect: The residual consistency term in the energy theorem is unsupported, and the H1 and L2 theorems reuse the same residual bound. Their stated estimates are consequently not proved for every load extension allowed by the old contract.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Amend the load-extension contract to require fδ=f on Ω and, for the Sobolev index used in the residual estimate, require the uniform compatibility bound ‖Δu^e+fδ‖_{H^s(Uδ(∂Ω))} ≤ C‖u^e‖_{H^{s+2}(Uδ(∂Ω))}. Use this stated premise at the residual step in the energy proof and in the reused H1 and L2 estimates.
issues.why_classification: This is a local compatibility condition on an auxiliary extension choice. Stating it makes the existing residual argument valid throughout the affected chain without changing the finite element method, conclusions, or convergence rates in the intended locally compatible extension regime; only extensions with unrelated exterior values are excluded.

issues.title: Missing domain-mismatch localization in the energy estimate
issues.failure_explanation: Restoring all old context includes both the boundary-error bounds and the paper-wide reverse boundary-proximity assumption. Those conditions do not state the nesting Omega subset Omega_delta required by the old mismatch lemma, nor does the proof derive the required localization of Omega_delta minus Omega relative to both boundaries. Consequently, the asserted inclusion and subsequent invocation of the lemma use an unestablished hypothesis.
issues.overall_effect: The energy estimate is not proved for all geometries admitted by its old assumptions. The H1 proof reuses the same mismatch argument, and the L2 proof uses both the energy theorem and the mismatch lemma.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add an explicit uniform domain-mismatch condition such as Ωδ△Ω ⊂ U_{Cδ}(∂Ω)∩U_{Cδ}(∂Ωδ), and restate the mismatch lemma for Ωδ∖Ω under this localization rather than under the unused nesting assumption Ω⊂Ωδ. Then apply that version in the energy, H1, and L2 proofs.
issues.why_classification: The repair is a standard local geometric-compatibility premise plus a routine adjustment of the strip lemma. It retains inward and outward signed boundary perturbations and leaves the method, estimates, and rates unchanged, while excluding only configurations that are not localized approximations of the same domain.

issues.title: Unbounded closest-point pullback in the H1 proof

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the function $u^e \circ q_\delta$ is constant along the normals to $\partial \Omega_\delta$

issues.failure_explanation: In local tubular coordinates, composing with q_delta maps u(x',t) to its trace u(x',0) and then extends that trace constantly in t. This rank-deficient map is not an ordinary Sobolev-preserving change of variables: a bulk H^s trace generally loses one-half derivative. Smooth functions with tangential frequency N and normal thickness N^{-1} make the output-to-input H^s norm ratio grow like N^{1/2}. Hence the asserted H^{p+1} bound and the interpolation estimates based on it are unjustified under the theorem's regularity assumptions.
issues.overall_effect: The estimate of boundary term I in the improved H1 theorem fails, so that theorem's stated bound is not established by the old proof. The L2 proof estimates its boundary term independently and does not rely on this pullback.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the claimed bulk H^{p+1} boundedness of the closest-point pullback. Instead prove a discrete dual-flux estimate ‖Σ_{nδ}(φ_h)‖_{H^{-1}(∂Ωδ)} ≤ C‖ψ‖_{L2(Ωδ)} using a uniform trace lifting, interpolation, stabilization, and discrete-dual stability. Pair this estimate with the valid boundary bound ‖u^e‖_{H^1(∂Ωδ)} ≤ C(δ‖u^e‖_{W^2∞}+δ_n‖u‖_{H^{p+1}}) to control term I and complete the H1 proof.
issues.why_classification: The rank-deficient pullback cannot be repaired by a notational edit or the asserted change-of-variables argument. Recovering the same H1 theorem requires a substantial replacement argument and a new boundary-flux lemma, but that work is contained to the boundary term and preserves the theorem's assumptions, conclusion, and rate.

issues.title: Geometry-rate guidance blurs sufficient conditions and necessity

failure_location.quote:
To recover optimal order convergence of order \(h^p\) in the \(H^1\)-seminorm, the geometric errors must therefore satisfy
\(\delta \lesssim h^p\) and \(\delta_n \lesssim h^p\).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The estimate in Theorem~\ref{thm:h1-error} shows that the boundary location error and the normal approximation error enter the \(H^1\)-seminorm additively, without the \(h^{-1/2}\)-amplification present in the energy norm estimate.

For the \(H^1\)-seminorm, the boundary location and normal approximation errors enter additively, and optimal order convergence of order \(h^p\) requires \(\delta \lesssim h^p\) and \(\delta_n \lesssim h^p\).

issues.failure_explanation: The remark is introduced as an interpretation of the preceding upper error estimate, so its natural estimate-based reading is that the displayed geometry scalings suffice to obtain the desired rate from that bound. But it says the errors must satisfy those scalings, and the numerical summary repeats them as requirements for convergence. This can reasonably be read as a necessity claim about actual convergence. The upper estimate supplies sufficient conditions, not such a converse. The issue is the unresolved distinction in the guidance, rather than a new defect in the displayed bound or an independently established necessity theorem that must be reconstructed.
issues.overall_effect: The practical guidance can mislead a reader about whether the stated geometry rates are sufficient conditions from the estimate or necessary conditions for convergence. This prose root does not itself invalidate the estimate; other issues affecting its proof are separate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace must/requires in the H1 remark and its repeated summary by an explicit statement that the displayed estimate guarantees optimal order provided delta and delta_n are O(h^p), under the stated hypotheses. Make clear that this is sufficient guidance derived from the upper bound and does not assert a converse. The prose repair requires no lower-bound proof and changes no displayed estimate.
issues.why_classification: Minor on the contextual reading: the paragraph already presents guidance obtained from a specific upper estimate, and the intended sufficient scalings and rate remain the same after clarification. The repeated necessity wording creates a real ambiguity rather than a uniquely forced typo, but resolving it requires only a local formulation change. If treated as an unequivocal independent necessity claim, withdrawal could justify moderate; that stronger interpretation is not adopted for this entry.

new_version_repair_locator.quote:
The estimate therefore guarantees optimal order convergence of order \(h^p\) in the \(H^1\)-seminorm provided that
\(\delta \lesssim h^p\) and \(\delta_n \lesssim h^p\).

issues.title: Unjustified uniform elliptic regularity in the L2 proof

failure_location.quote: Since \(\partial\Omega_\delta\) is assumed smooth, the dual solution \(\phi\) satisfies the elliptic regularity estimate

issues.failure_explanation: For the asymptotic L2 estimate, the hidden constant in the dual H2 bound must remain independent of h and delta. Smoothness of each individual approximate boundary only supports a domain-dependent estimate and does not control a family with degenerating reach, curvature, or other regularity constants. The old theorem contains no uniform elliptic-regularity hypothesis, so the uniform premise used by its proof is unestablished.
issues.overall_effect: The constant in the claimed L2 estimate may depend uncontrollably on the approximate domain, so the old proof does not establish a uniform convergence estimate as delta and h vary.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add to the L2 theorem an explicit uniform elliptic-regularity hypothesis: for every relevant δ and every g∈L2(Ωδ), the Dirichlet solution of −Δφ=g satisfies ‖φ‖_{H2(Ωδ)}≤C‖g‖_{L2(Ωδ)} with C independent of h, δ, and the cut configuration. Invoke this uniform estimate at each duality step.
issues.why_classification: Uniform H2 regularity is a standard technical qualification for an Aubin–Nitsche argument on a varying domain family. Making it explicit is short and routine and leaves the L2 conclusion and rate unchanged for the intended uniformly regular smooth-domain regime.

issues.title: Undefined extension of the approximate-domain dual solution

diagnostic_evidence.quote: let \(\phi \in H^1_0(\Omega_\delta)\) solve the dual problem

issues.failure_explanation: The old operator E and the notation v^e are defined only for functions on the exact domain Omega. The dual solution belongs to H^1_0(Omega_delta), yet the proof uses pi_h phi^e and bounds its interpolation error on the active mesh. No extension of phi from Omega_delta, and no uniform H2 stability for such an extension, is defined or assumed. Thus a required proof object and estimate are missing.
issues.overall_effect: The interpolation and stabilization bounds for the dual solution are undefined, leaving the L2 duality proof incomplete independently of the separate elliptic-regularity defect.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Introduce uniformly bounded approximate-domain extension operators Eδ:H^2(Ωδ)→H^2(R^d), define φ^e=Eδφ, and state that the extension constant is independent of δ. Use this extension on the active mesh in every interpolation and stabilization estimate involving the dual solution.
issues.why_classification: The missing object is supplied by a standard uniform extension premise for a regular domain family. Once it is stated, the existing interpolation and stabilization calculations become well-defined without a new proof mechanism or any change to the L2 theorem's conclusion or convergence rate.
